claims.text: The first rules anybody writes for an agent are mechanical and the same in every company: do not send email, only draft it; do not delete anything; use your own account.
claims.quote: They are short, they are the same in every company, and they are the rules I wrote first

claims.text: A few questions in, which drafts may be sent, to whom, whether a price may be mentioned, you are no longer describing an agent but the business.
claims.quote: A few questions in, you are no longer describing an agent. You are describing the business.

claims.text: Below the first layer or two of an Agent Behaviour Policy what is captured is business logic, much of it never written down, which the agent-control tools stop before and which decides whether an agent can be trusted with real work.
claims.quote: The tools that sell agent controls mostly stop before it.

claims.text: The mechanical layers are boundaries enforced by something the agent's grant does not include: its own account, the platform holding the token, deletion switched off, outside forwarding blocked, sending needing a person.
claims.quote: Secrets held by the platform rather than the agent, tools switched off rather than discouraged, an identity per agent rather than a shared login

claims.text: When the agent operating a Google Workspace mailbox measured its connector on 19 September it found thirty tools, and send_message ran with no prompt while trashing a message stopped for approval; mechanics take measurement.
claims.quote: The mechanics are where a policy starts, and getting them right takes measurement, not reading the documentation.

claims.text: Above the mechanics are four business layers: the function, how this firm does email; the process, the steps work goes through; the relationship, who this customer is to us now; and the organisation, what the company is for.
claims.quote: Go one layer up and the rules stop being the same in every company.

claims.text: The process layer includes a complaint reaching a named person within one working hour, an invoice going out only after finance approval, and no email telling a candidate a hiring outcome.
claims.quote: A complaint reaches a named person within one working hour.

value.unit: working hour for a complaint to reach a named person

claims.text: Each layer has a different owner: IT and security, the head of operations, finance and HR and legal, the account managers, the board.
claims.quote: each layer has a different owner: IT and security, the head of operations, finance and HR and legal, the account managers, the board

claims.text: A vendor that models each customer's business becomes a consultancy and one that does not sells the bottom of the stack; the mechanical layer is a product and the business layers are the customer's to write.
claims.quote: The mechanical layer is a product. The business layers are the customer's, and the customer has to write them.

claims.text: Companies never wrote the business logic down because their software was the law: approval chains, role-based access, field-level permissions and workflow engines encode it, and privacy decisions live there.
claims.quote: Their software was the law.

claims.text: An agent works through APIs, not screens, and can call the endpoint the button would have called, so the rule the interface enforced by omission is no longer enforced unless written down and enforced.
claims.quote: The rule that the user interface enforced by omission is no longer enforced, unless somebody writes it down and something enforces it.

claims.text: The structure that holds this is fractal: behaviour policies inside behaviour policies, each layer refining the one below inside the room it allows, from foundational controls up to what the company is for.
claims.quote: behaviour policies inside behaviour policies, each layer refining the one below, inside the room the one below allows

claims.text: The top layer is the company's to define, fair treatment or maximum revenue; a behaviour policy describes and does not judge, but a written one can be read and shown.
claims.quote: That top layer is the company's to define.

claims.text: The ABP's own vocabulary is three layers, shared facts owned by nobody, each party's formulas and declared bridges, and a customer extends it by adding nodes in its own vault.
claims.quote: A customer extends it by adding nodes in its own vault, never by asking for a change in ours.

claims.text: For every rule the policy records which of four things stands in the way: nothing, an expectation in prose enforced by nobody, a setting the agent's own account can flip, or a boundary; only the boundary is a control.
claims.quote: Only the last is a control.

claims.text: Adding whether a named person has accepted the risk with an expiry puts every rule in one of three states: backed by a control, governed by an accepted risk, or resting on hope.
claims.quote: every rule lands in one of three states: backed by a control, governed by an accepted risk, or resting on hope

claims.text: In the fictional example five of the seventeen rules are backed by a control, six by an accepted risk and six are hope; the platform layer is all control and the organisation layer all hope.
claims.quote: five of the seventeen rules are backed by a control, six are governed by an accepted risk, and six are hope

claims.text: Resting on hope is not a failure, since most of a business has always run on people behaving as asked, but with an agent it can be counted.
claims.quote: most of a business has always run on people behaving as asked

claims.text: The behaviour policy is a good place for vendors to integrate rather than a threat: a vendor enforces the parts of the written policy its product can reach, and several vendors can each own a row.
claims.quote: it gives their controls a rule to enforce and a number to move

claims.text: A send gateway moves a new recipient needs a person from accepted risk to control, an outbound content check moves never quote a price from hope to control, and a control attached to a written rule is worth more than one switched on in general.
claims.quote: A control attached to a written rule is worth more than one switched on in general, because the customer can see what it bought.

claims.text: The AI Baseline Control Framework asks in RG.2 that what an autonomous AI system does is described and in AC.3 that it has a named owner; the description is the layers above the mechanics and the owner the name on each layer.
claims.quote: The description RG.2 asks for is the layers above the mechanics.

claims.text: The upper layers look like a skill: a skill says how, a policy layer says what is allowed, who owns the rule and what stands in the way of breaking it, and together they are the business codified for an agent.
claims.quote: A skill says how. A policy layer says what is allowed, who owns the rule, and what stands in the way of breaking it.

claims.text: Writing it down lets the business scale: knowledge in a few heads and in software nobody could read becomes something an agent can follow, a person can review and a control can enforce.
claims.quote: something an agent can follow, a person can review and a control can enforce

claims.text: Next: take the measured Gmail deployment as the bottom two layers, write the function, process and relationship layers for one real inbox, count the three states, publish as a vault with its read key, then repeat with a vendor's control in the path.
claims.quote: Then do it again with a vendor's control in the path, and publish the count before and after.

claims.text: The example is fictional on purpose so the shape is clear; the firm, its rules and its counts are illustrative.
claims.quote: The example here is fictional on purpose, so the shape is clear.

claims.text: The proportions in the hope figure are illustrative; the shape is the point.
claims.quote: The proportions are illustrative; the shape is the point.

claims.text: The kinds of product named in the third figure are categories, not recommendations, and no vendor was contacted.
claims.quote: are categories, not recommendations, and no vendor was contacted
